summary: Groups content and actions about one thing (a release, a project, a pull request), with an optional header and footer.

children: Adds a subtle Badge appearance and tightens focus styles. Two components changed, no token changes.

whenToUse: A self-contained object shown in a collection: a release, a project, a pull request.
A summary the user scans before opening the detail page.
A settings section that benefits from a visible boundary.
whenNotToUse: Only to add padding or a border around page content: use spacing and layout instead.
Cards inside cards: flatten with headings and dividers.
Making the whole card one click target that also contains buttons: nested interactive elements trap keyboard and screen reader users.

dos.title: Header names the thing, footer holds the actions
dos.text: Users scan titles, then act. Keep at most one primary action in the footer.

children: Two components changed, no token changes.

dos.title: Status goes in the header, next to the title
dos.text: The badge is read right after the name, which is where users look for it.

children: CSS variables generated for light and dark themes.

donts.title: A card inside a card
donts.text: Double borders and shadows add noise and make the hierarchy harder to read, especially in dark mode.

donts.title: A footer full of actions
donts.text: Four equal buttons means no decision was made. Pick one main action, move the rest to the detail page.

accessibility: A card is a plain container with no role. When it is a section users may want to jump to, give it a title in the header and, in code, point aria-labelledby at that title.
Use the same heading level for every card title in a list, so the page outline stays flat and predictable.
The edge is drawn by both a border and elevation.raised. In dark mode the shadow is stronger so the edge stays visible.
Reading and focus order follow the markup: header, body, footer. Do not reorder visually.
